newsitem.title: SPAIN: Poor weather still delaying North Spain harvest.
newsitem.headline: Poor weather still delaying North Spain harvest.

text.p: Harvesting of barley and soft wheat in Spain's key Castille-Leon region is still being held back by wet weather, local farmers' associations said on Monday.
"The harvesting is still being delayed because we haven't had the right weather. It's been damp and there's more rain forecast," a technical expert at young farmers' association ASAJA told Reuters.
He estimated that around one third of the barley crop has been collected. A minimum amount of wheat has been brought in, although harvesting has barely started, he said.
But so far the overall outlook was relatively good.
"Quality is normal, although we don't know that much yet. But no-one's saying the harvest is a bad one," he said.
It was still early to make predictions on maize, he said, as it is still in a primary phase.
Castille-Leon, the main area for Spanish grains, produced around 2.1 million tonnes of soft wheat and about 4.6 million tonnes of barley in 1996, according to Agriculture Ministry estimates.
Latest official forecasts for this year see the region producing 1.5 million tonnes of wheat and 3.0 million tonnes of barley, ASAJA said.
Spain's total output of barley and wheat this year is expected to be around 12.76 million tonnes, May official forecasts show, versus 16.8 million tonnes in 1996.
